race_context: Indianapolis Public Schools (IPS) serves central Indianapolis in Marion County. State data showed 19,774 students in 2025-26, down 6% from the prior year; Chalkbeat counted just under 31,000 across IPS's full portfolio including Innovation Network schools {cb_enrollment}. The superintendent is Aleesia Johnson {cb_referendum}.

The Board of School Commissioners has seven members: five elected from geographic districts and two at-large {wfyi_candidates}. Districts 2, 3 and 5 cover the northern half of IPS (east, central and west respectively) and District 4 the southwest; any IPS voter may vote in the at-large race, and only district residents vote in district races {cb_guide}.

Five seats are on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot, each electing one member: the regularly scheduled District 3, District 5 and one at-large seat, plus Districts 2 and 4, which were filled by appointment after resignations {cb_guide}. The state list's "vote for 1" for the at-large race matches this {in_list}.

Incumbents: District 2, Hasaan Rashid (appointed March 2026 after Gayle Cosby resigned); District 3, board president Hope Duke Star; District 4, Chris Bultman (appointed June 2026 after Allissa Impink resigned); District 5, vice president Nicole Carey; at-large, Angelia Lois Moore. All five are seeking election {wfyi_candidates} {cb_guide}. The District 4 winner serves the rest of Impink's term through 2028 {cb_d4_interviews}.

2026 is the first election in which Indiana school board candidates may list a party; school board races are not part of straight-ticket voting, and candidates of the same party can run against each other {cb_guide}.

Governance change: under a state law passed in early 2026, the mayor-appointed Indianapolis Public Education Corporation (IPEC) took over buildings, transportation and the power to place a tax measure on the ballot for IPS and city charter schools; the elected board sets policy and goals, makes some financial decisions, and hires and oversees the superintendent {cb_d2_interviews} {cb_referendum} {cb_guide}.

Budget: WFYI reported in June 2026 a projected deficit of roughly $40 million and about $24 million already cut {wfyi_candidates}. IPS expects about $20 million more in cuts even if the November referendum passes, and $40 million to $45 million in cuts, plus possible state intervention, if it fails {cb_referendum}.

Referendum: IPEC placed a four-year operating referendum of up to about 37 cents per $100 of assessed value on the Nov. 3 ballot, expected to raise about $95 million a year, split roughly half to IPS and half among about 60 participating charters; it would replace IPS's 2018 referendum, which expires this year {cb_referendum}. The Indianapolis Education Association voted not to support it because IPS would still face cuts {cb_referendum}. Chalkbeat noted the 2025 state property tax changes limit future district revenue {cb_referendum}.
Enrollment: IPS's 2025-26 decline was its largest since the pandemic, according to Chalkbeat's analysis of state data {cb_enrollment}.

Ballot-access dispute (District 4): the county election board removed Lindsey Cornett in August over her Democratic affiliation; a Marion Superior Court judge restored her on Sept. 11 without a party label {wfyi_cornett_removed} {cb_cornett_restored}.

Forums: Chalkbeat Indiana and WFYI will host a candidate forum Oct. 19 at the Indianapolis Public Library Central Branch; they also sent all candidates survey questions for their Sept. 10 voter guide {cb_guide}.

Points of difference in reviewed coverage include views on IPEC (Duarte and Cornett emphasize holding it accountable; Star cites guiding its implementation), charter-district relations (Bultman and Rashid stress collaboration across school types; Carey raised a conflict concern about Bultman's charter employer), and party labels (Redelman and Houston chose independent status) {wfyi_candidates} {cb_d4_interviews} {cb_bultman_appt}.

candidates.summary: Assistant professor at the Purdue University College of Education, running as a Democrat; he was runner-up when the board filled the vacant District 2 seat in March 2026 {wfyi_candidates} {cb_rashid_appt}.
background: Assistant professor of educational leadership and policy at Purdue University; he has said his comments and interest in the seat do not reflect the university {cb_d2_interviews}.
Former teacher with an educational research background {cb_d2_interviews}.
First in his family born in the U.S. and to attend college {wfyi_candidates}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as a Democrat {in_list}. He said he filed as a Democrat because it most closely aligns with how he votes, though he does not believe school board races should be partisan {wfyi_candidates}.
Applied for the District 2 vacancy in March 2026; the board chose Hasaan Rashid 4-2, with Allissa Impink and Nicole Carey voting for Duarte {cb_rashid_appt}.

items: Said the biggest challenge facing IPS is that its fiscal future "falls at the mercy of the mayor-appointed IPEC," which he described as made up of people with a stake in schools not fully run by IPS {wfyi_candidates}.

Said IPS has been good stewards of taxpayer dollars, that state legislation has adversely affected the district, and that the district must ensure budget cuts do not worsen inequalities {cb_d2_interviews}.
Told the board he would set aside differences between school types and focus on student outcomes {cb_d2_interviews}.
Said: "I'm unwilling to compromise on meeting the needs of the people who have historically been left out of choice" {cb_d2_interviews}.
Has advocated in public meetings for a fully elected school board and questioned the creation of the Indianapolis Public Education Corporation {cb_d2_interviews}.

on_incumbent: Has questioned the state law that created IPEC and moved powers away from the elected board {cb_d2_interviews} {cb_rashid_appt}.
plans: Said he is running to hold public schools accountable {wfyi_candidates}.
endorsements_finance: Chalkbeat reported that in the March appointment, Duarte was backed by traditional public school supporters; he cited his work with the IPS Parent Council {cb_rashid_appt}.
gaps: No campaign finance reports (Marion County Election Board filings) were reviewed; fundraising is unknown.
